title: Statistics - Lesson 7: Deciles and Percentiles Practice
description: Practice ordering data, calculating decile and percentile locators, interpolating values, and interpreting results.

questions.question: Before finding a decile or percentile for ungrouped data, what should you do first?
options: Order the data from least to greatest
Round every value to the nearest ten
Divide the largest value by the smallest value
questions.explanation: Deciles and percentiles are measures of position, so the positions only make sense after the data are ordered.

questions.question: Which percentile is equivalent to the sixth decile, D6?
questions.explanation: Each decile represents ten percentile points, so D6 is the same position as P60.

questions.question: For a data set with n = 9, what is the locator for D4? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: For a decile, L = k(n + 1)/10. Thus L = 4(9 + 1)/10 = 4.

questions.question: Use the ordered data 12, 18, 20, 25, 31, 36, 40, 44, 50. What is D4?
questions.explanation: There are 9 values, so L = 4(10)/10 = 4. The 4th ordered value is 25.

questions.question: For n = 11, what is the locator for P25? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: For a percentile, L = k(n + 1)/100. Thus L = 25(12)/100 = 3.

questions.question: A locator is L = 6.5. What should you do?
options: Interpolate halfway between the 6th and 7th values
questions.explanation: A locator of 6.5 is halfway between positions 6 and 7, so interpolation is needed.

questions.question: The 5th ordered value is 42 and the 6th ordered value is 50. If L = 5.25, what is the interpolated value? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: Move 0.25 of the way from 42 to 50: 42 + 0.25(8) = 44.

questions.question: In one sentence, interpret P80 = 72 for a set of test scores.
questions.correctAnswer: In this set of test scores, about 80% of the ordered score positions are at or below 72.
questions.explanation: A good interpretation names the data context, the percentile level, and the cut point value.
